messages.author: 2fc2adf03df964eb
messages.subject: Re: obtaining predicted values of latents in Lavaan
parts:
Thank you for the link!

So the approach would be something like this:

#Create frame with IDs
CFA_Used<-data.frame(inspect(fit, "case.idx"))
CFA_Used$used<- 1
names(CFA_Used) <- c("ID", "used")

#Keep only the used IDs in Main Data Frame
MyData$ID<-as.numeric(rownames(MyData))
MyData<-merge(MyData,CFA_Used, by="ID")
MyData<-subset(MyData, used==1)

#Paste data together
MyData<-cbind(MyData, predict(fit))

It's not really a safer approach though: a change in sort order of MyData (though not likely) would not paste them together properly. You'd need ID variables for the Factorscores as well.

messages.subject: Re: obtaining predicted values of latents in Lavaan
parts:
On 10/15/2015 09:16 PM, Paul Hofman wrote:
> It's not really a safer approach though: a change in sort order of
> MyData (though not likely) would not paste them together properly. You'd
> need ID variables for the Factorscores as well.

Why not use the newdata= argument of predict/lavPredict? First fit the
model. Then, construct a new dataset called, say, Data2, perhaps
omitting all incomplete cases (and optionally reordering the cases).
Then, you can safely use

cbind(Data2, lavPredict(fit, newdata = Data2) )

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: obtaining predicted values of latents in Lavaan
parts:
On 11/07/2015 10:43 AM, stefanwa...@gmail.com wrote:
> Does lavaan store an "imputed" exposure/determinant matrix somewhere?

No. When missing="ml" (or "fiml"), the NA values are ignored, and the
case-wise likelihoods are computed using the non-missing values only;
nothing is imputed.

Having said this, it is possible to compute factor scores in the
presence of missing data, but this is not (yet) implemented in lavaan
(0.5-20). It is on my TODO list.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: obtaining predicted values of latents in Lavaan
parts: I guess that this problem is related with the degrees of freedom.

Degrees of freedom in covariance structure analysis are not calculated from sample size.  If you are missing factor scores for 2 of your observations, I'm guessing those 2 observations have missing values on at least one of the indicators.
How can I get the predicted values for all my observations?

lavaan does not provide factor scores for cases with missing values.  But the development version does return rows with NA for those rows of the data, so you should be able to match the factor scores to the correct cases.

install.packages("lavaan", repos = "http://www.da.ugent.be", type = "source")

parts: Just a quick comment about the factor scores with missing data. When factor scores are requested in blavaan it does provide the factor scores for every subject, even if they had missing data. This is because in MCMC missing data is treated as imputations at each iteration of the MCMC. So the factor scores requested are the mean of all factor scores from the posterior distributions

On another note: Is it valid to used these predicted values of latent variables in other (multilevel) analysis as a dependent variable?

Not unless you account for the uncertainty of the estimated factor-score values.  I would use blavaan like Mauricio suggested.  You can obtain a posterior distribution of factor scores for each person, which you can treat as multiple imputations if you want to use them as "observed variables" in a subsequent analysis.  semTools::runMI() makes it convenient to fit lavaan models to multiple imputations and pool results.

https://www.statmodel.com/download/Plausible.pdf

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: obtaining predicted values of latents in Lavaan
parts:
Another way to account for the uncertainty of the factor scores is to get the posterior distributions of factor scores from blavaan. And then use brms with the measurement error feautres, you specify the mean of the posteriors as the estimated variable, and the standard deviation from the posterior distributions as the measurement error devaitions. Here is a toy example on how to specify this in brms

library(brms)
library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

N <- 100
dat <- data.frame(
  y = rnorm(N), x1 = rnorm(N),
  x2 = rnorm(N), sdx1 = abs(rnorm(N, 1)), sdx2 = abs(rnorm(N, 1)),
  sdy=abs(rnorm(N, 1))
)
head(dat)

# fit a simple error-in-variables model
# | se(sdy) = measurement error in the outcome
# me(x1, sdx) = measurement error in variable x1 with standard deviation sdx
fit1 <- brm(y | se(sdy, sigma=TRUE) ~ me(x1, sdx1) + me(x2, sdx2), data = dat,
            save_mevars = TRUE, chains = 3, iter=8000)
summary(fit1)
